_note: Lift and throughput for closure (when the last ton arrives); see lift.py and the Lift layer spec in the Program Hub. Change a figure here and nothing else: no code change is needed. Every figure has a source in the shape falcon_data.py checks: status sourced (read from a page that was opened), unverified (a source is named but its page wasn't opened) or illustrative (chosen for the demo, not a planning factor). Stage 1: the starting set sits at the origin, ready on D+0.

ships._note: Capacity in short tons only; deck area is not modelled (decided 25 Nov 2026). Sailing time is the route's, at the carrier speed in movement_rules.json; the ship type sets only how much one load carries. carrier is who sails it (movement_rules.json): commercial carriers keep out of a WEZ when sailing to the loading port.

capacity_st.source: Chosen for the demo. For reference only, not used: 312,461 sq ft of deck (T-AKR 295)

aircraft._note: Planning payload (allowable cabin load), not the maximum in air_rules.json: planners use it on long legs. Ground hours are per stop, block-in to block-out.

planning_payload_st.source: A Gemini summary of AFPAM 10-1403 gave 75 to 85 short tons; no table or page given

ground_hours.source: The same Gemini summary gave 4 to 6 hours

planning_payload_st.source: The same Gemini summary gave '145.0 short tons (~90,000 lbs)'; 90,000 lb is 45 short tons, the figure used

ground_hours.source: The same Gemini summary gave 2.25 to 3.25 hours

plan._note: The baseline movement plan: each class's normal mode, before any what-if changes it. Who flies it (commercial or military aircraft) comes from air_rules.json. Fuel is shown in gallons as well as short tons.

normal_mode.source: After a Gemini summary of how planners split a manifest between sealift and airlift: fuel and heavy cargo by sea; rations, spares, personal items and medical by commercial air; ammunition by military air. Class VIII by any aircraft, as in air_rules.json, pending Ben's call

fuel_lb_per_gal.source: About 6.7 lb a gallon for military jet fuel, from the same Gemini summary

ports._note: Short tons a day a port can load or discharge, by World Port Index harbor size (the WPI has no rates). '' is a port with no size. A sourced rate for one port goes in port_rates.csv and wins over these.

airfields._note: Working MOG: aircraft an airfield can load or unload at once, by OurAirports type. Sorties a day = working MOG x 24 / ground hours.
